label: 0048 · Smoothed in time, 1997–2025 (one QP over 48 windows): 0047 with a heavy-tailed background calibrated on null runs, uncorrelated noise, background coupling from −1 to 1, eleven slow slip events as signal, fixed 747-site network, UNR positions (MAP)
description: 0047 with a heavy-tailed background. Where a roughly 100 km patch's change in background coupling into a window of at least 180 days exceeds 1.07 prior sd, its prior is relaxed (log tail), so a large change costs little more than one of that size. The threshold is the largest such change in three runs on data with no background change (0047's solution with its background held constant plus its real residuals moved between windows); on fresh runs of that kind, noise alone relaxes 0–4 patch-windows. The real data relax 31: the southern Japan Trench off Boso and beneath Ibaraki in 2004–09, the Bungo Channel in 2004, shallow off Kii and Tokai after the September 2004 off-Kii earthquakes, Hyuga-nada in 2021–22, beneath Ise Bay in 2017–18 and the Kuril trench (strike-slip) in 2006–07. The fit improves by only 0.5% in those windows, several of the largest changes are far offshore or in strike-slip and swing between windows, and the reweighting had not converged after six passes, so read the relaxed changes as candidates, not measurements. Changes planted into the data are recovered as by 0047 (66–93% of a 0.3 drop near the coast). Block rotations are 0047's. Coupling far outside −1 to 1 isn't a real value: it is episode strike-slip, or Kumamoto afterslip, divided by a small plate rate. MAP solution, no posterior SD.
